findings.reason: a node dispatched on §6 must name the mechanism it serialises on, and the plan names one that does not exist; the plan's own v5 review comment (c-20261023-s6-lock) records the same defect as unresolved, and v6 did not correct the sentence.
findings.text: §6 rests its serialisation design on "the landing lock" (`runs the same crew land path a coordinator calls, serialised per repository under the landing lock`) and no object of that name exists in the tree; landings serialise on the checkout's `.git/index.lock` retry path (`reckon/crew/merge.py:481` `_index_lock_held`, `:485` `_run_waiting_out_a_held_index_lock`) and on the per-run promotion lease in `reckon/crew/promotion.py`, so the driver node would either invent a lock or duplicate an existing one

findings.reason: the finding is not the number but the instrument; the gate must name the MCP read it times, or state a shell-level bound, or it cannot be scored by whoever runs it (and the unresolved v5 comment c-20261023-s3-deadline asks exactly this).
findings.text: §3's done-when measures "`crew view live` and the obligations view each answer within that 30 s deadline, cold and warm", but the 30 s figure is `READ_DEADLINE_SECONDS` applied by the MCP read wrapper (`reckon/mcp_deadlines.py:45,444`), which bounds MCP tool calls and not a shell invocation of the crew CLI, so the node cannot tell which instrument the gate means and the measure can pass or fail for reasons outside the code under test

findings.reason: a node dispatched on §4 would be sent to edit another project's router, and would find its two instructions incompatible; the router has one reader to satisfy, and §4's own done-when (a request not held on `admission.sessions[<session>].worker_slots`) is fully satisfied by the second sentence alone.
findings.text: §4 states in one sentence that "the lane router in imas-ambix then publishes one figure ... and stops dividing it by session (`admission.sessions`, `fair_share`)" and in the next that "the router's per-session figures go unused but stay published until imas-ambix drops them", so the section declares both a change and a non-change to the same publisher, and the change it declares is in imas-ambix, a different repository than the one the section's write paths sit in

findings.reason: the followup is the sentence a coordinator schedules the wave from, and it names as parallel the two sections whose declared edges forbid that; either the sentence or the edges is wrong, and only the author knows which.
findings.text: followup `f-aqhwp-001` tells the coordinator "§5 and §7 can run beside it", while the plan's own `plan-section-depends-on` declares s5 depends on s2 and s7 depends on s4, which depends on s5, so both transitively wait on §2 and neither may launch before it lands

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: a finding — §6 names "the landing lock" as the object that serialises landings, and no such object exists in the repository.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §3's done-when times `crew view live` against the 30 s deadline that only the MCP read wrapper applies.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §2 places every log under the run directory, which is the durable crew run store, and no section writes evidence to a node-local or session path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the proposed states (`awaiting-upstream`, `blocked-upstream`), the configuration key and the new verbs are named by mechanism, and no plan label, stage name or ticket number reaches a symbol, filename or comment.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §4's mechanism is self-contradictory: one sentence moves the per-session slot split out of the lane router and the next keeps the router's per-session figures, and the first sentence requires a change in imas-ambix, another repository.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — each of §2–§7 names one deliverable with one gate; §5's three queue verbs serve the single deliverable of an editable queued request.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — every `plan-section-depends-on` ref resolves to a section that exists (s3→s2,s4; s4→s5; s5→s2; s6→s2; s7→s4), but the followup's scheduling sentence contradicts those edges.
